s1.syndrome_frame: cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias in a patient with metastatic cancer
salient_findings: single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque on the lower right lateral shin
discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels on histopathological analysis
key_facts: male patient in his 40s
weight: 109kg
diagnosed with stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma in November 2013
pulmonary and liver metastases
treated with radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
enrolled in trial E7208 at the Smilow Cancer Hospital at Yale-New Haven
received combination therapy every 2 weeks
developed a cutaneous lesion in early January 2015
lesion was 4 cm in diameter and not associated with pain or pruritus
histopathological analysis showed superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels
epidermis was normal
paired whole-exome sequencing of affected tissue and patient's blood was performed

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: cutaneous lesion with telangiectasias in a patient with metastatic cancer

shortlist.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: association with lymphedema and metastatic cancer

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: cutaneous vascular lesion in a patient with immunosuppression

shortlist.label: Pseudo-Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: similar clinical presentation to Kaposi's sarcoma

shortlist.label: Atypical vascular lesion
shortlist.why_kept: histopathological findings of superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels

raw.rationale: The patient's cutaneous lesion is characterized by superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels and a normal epidermis, which is consistent with an atypical vascular lesion. Additionally, the presence of a KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Angiosarcoma typically presents with more aggressive features, such as rapid growth and invasion, which are not described in this case.

rejected.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
rejected.why: Stewart-Treves syndrome is a type of angiosarcoma that occurs in the setting of chronic lymphedema, which is not mentioned in this case.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Kaposi's sarcoma typically presents with multiple lesions and is associated with human herpesvirus 8 infection, which is not mentioned in this case.

rejected.label: Pseudo-Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Pseudo-Kaposi's sarcoma is a type of vascular lesion that occurs in the setting of chronic venous insufficiency, which is not described in this case.
